steps.title: Create an admin account with sudo and the keys of an existing account

edits.new:
# Written by stackward: plan step admin-user, the admin account.
# NOPASSWD because the account has no password; stackward never sets one.
# Remove this file to take the rights away.
ops ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL
edits.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/etc/sudoers.d/90-stackward-ops
@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+# Written by stackward: plan step admin-user, the admin account.
+# NOPASSWD because the account has no password; stackward never sets one.
+# Remove this file to take the rights away.
+ops ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL

commands.why: create the account with a home and its own group; its password stays locked
create ~/.ssh, owned by the account, mode 0700
copy the authorized keys of ubuntu (/home/ubuntu/.ssh/authorized_keys) on the host, so no key passes through the plan

undo.description: Remove the sudoers drop-in and delete the account ops with its home and group (userdel --remove). Anything saved in that home is deleted with it.

commands.why: delete the account, its home and its group

notes: The keys come from ubuntu (/home/ubuntu/.ssh/authorized_keys), copied on the host; nothing is changed there.
ops gets sudo without a password (NOPASSWD), like the cloud image's default account; USR-004 lists it. Set a password and drop NOPASSWD later if you prefer.
Prove it before you confirm: open a new SSH session as ops with the key of ubuntu and run sudo stackward confirm from there.
lock-default-user is planned once a session of this account applies it.

steps.title: Allow key logins only, refuse root and limit auth tries with an early sshd drop-in

edits.new:
# Written by stackward: plan step sshd-hardening, fixes SSH-001, SSH-003, SSH-005.
# Named to sort first: sshd keeps the first value it reads. Remove this
# file and reload ssh.service to undo.
PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
MaxAuthTries 3
edits.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-stackward-hardening.conf
@@ -0,0 +1,6 @@
+# Written by stackward: plan step sshd-hardening, fixes SSH-001, SSH-003, SSH-005.
+# Named to sort first: sshd keeps the first value it reads. Remove this
+# file and reload ssh.service to undo.
+PasswordAuthentication no
+PermitRootLogin no
+MaxAuthTries 3

commands.why: load the new settings; running sessions stay open

undo.description: Remove the drop-in and reload ssh.service; the earlier values return for new logins.

notes: sshd runs under socket activation (ssh.socket); the drop-in sets no port or listen address, so reloading ssh.service is enough and ssh.socket is left alone.
Existing SSH sessions stay open. Before you confirm, log in again in a new session with your key: that is the proof the change works.
Ubuntu 22.04 and later and Debian 12 and later; older OpenSSH reads KbdInteractiveAuthentication differently.
